case: A transition nothing pinned is removed, and the lifecycle is still coherent, so it must not be refused.
why: The transition table pins routes whose ABSENCE changes a safety property. It is not a closed enumeration of every lifecycle, and reading it as one would turn a floor under the registry into a freeze on it. Here `ContextManifest: admitted -> invalidated` is removed and `invalidated` remains reachable from `captured`, so no phase is lost and no guard is orphaned. A control that refused this would refuse ordinary registry work, and the adverse count beside it could not be read as a detection rate.
